name: Dr. Rohan, the Resident Doctor
tagline: Years of study, a big loan, and a long climb to a good income.
story: First doctor in the family. The years of study left a loan and little else, and a junior resident's pay does not stretch far. The climb to a specialist's income is steep and sure, but it takes a while, and a lot rides on the loan being paid in time.

job_loss.name: Hospital cutbacks
job_loss.story: The hospital cut its posts and you were between jobs for {months} months. The next post paid {pct}% less.

job_offer.name: A better post
job_offer.story: A bigger hospital offered you a better post. Your pay jumped {pct}%.

provenance.basis: Illustrative: a junior resident in a tier-2 city carrying a 15 lakh education loan, mid-2020s. Pay growth of 10% a year (nominal, about 5.5 points above inflation) stands for the climb from resident to specialist; a real specialist's income is far more uneven than this. The loan is a game number, not a typical figure.
